name: Grade 2
theme: Forgiveness and the Eucharist: preparing for first sacraments

lessons.title: Made in God’s image
lessons.idea: God made us with a body and a soul. We can think, choose and love. This makes us different from the animals.
lessons.question: What can people do that animals cannot?
lessons.activity: Draw a self-portrait and list three gifts God gave you.
teach: We have a body and a soul. The soul lives forever (CCC 362–366). We can think, choose and love.
We are made in God’s image (Genesis 1:26–27; CCC 355).
Celebrate differences: everyone is made in God’s image.
talk: What can you do that your pet cannot?
How can you take care of your body and your soul?
quiz: People are made of…|Body and soul|Only body|Only soul|Clay only|0|CCC 362.
The soul…|Dies with the body|Lives forever|Is a feeling|Is a thought|1|CCC 366.
We are made in God’s…|Shadow|Image|House|Costume|1|Genesis 1:27.
lessons.life: Thank God each morning for your body and your soul.
lessons.saint: Francis de Sales: he taught that a happy heart honors God.
lessons.mem: God made me in his image. (Genesis 1:27)
lessons.hook: Look in a mirror. Ask, “What can you do that a dog can’t?”
lessons.assess: Ask: “What are two gifts God gave you?”

lessons.title: Free to choose
lessons.idea: God gave us free will. We can choose good or evil. When we choose good, we grow in goodness.
lessons.question: What is a good choice you made this week?
lessons.activity: Sort “good choice” and “bad choice” cards and explain why.
teach: Free will lets us choose good or evil (CCC 1730–1731). God wants us to choose love freely.
Deuteronomy 30:19: “Choose life.”
Link choices to growing in goodness.
talk: What good choice did you make this week?
quiz: Free will lets us…|Be forced|Choose|Hide|Forget|1|CCC 1731.
Good choices lead to…|Nothing|Happiness and goodness|Sadness|Trouble|1|CCC 1733.
Who helps us choose well?|Nobody|God, family, the Church|Only a screen|Only friends|1|CCC 1783.
lessons.life: Before you decide something this week, say a quick prayer: “Jesus, help me choose well.”
lessons.saint: Aloysius Gonzaga: he chose to give up his inheritance to serve God.
lessons.mem: Choose life. (Deuteronomy 30:19)
lessons.hook: Hold two paths drawn on paper. “You choose which way.”
lessons.assess: Ask for an example of a good choice and a bad choice.

lessons.title: Sin hurts and God heals
lessons.idea: Sin hurts our friendship with God and others. God never stops loving us. He sent Jesus to save us.
lessons.question: How did the father welcome the son?
lessons.activity: Act out the Prodigal Son. Say, “Welcome home.”
teach: Sin hurts our friendship with God and others (CCC 1846, 1850). God never stops loving us.
The Prodigal Son (Luke 15:11–32): the father runs to welcome his son.
Emphasize mercy first.
talk: How did the father welcome his son?
What does God do when we come home?
quiz: The father in the story…|Ran to welcome his son|Closed the door|Scolded him|Sent him away|0|Luke 15:20.
The father is like…|God|A judge|A stranger|A teacher|0|CCC 1439.
Sin hurts…|Only us|Nobody|Only teachers|Our friendship with God and others|3|CCC 1850.
lessons.life: If you did something wrong this week, say, “I’m sorry” to the person and to God.
lessons.saint: Dismas: the good thief who was welcomed into paradise.
lessons.mem: My child, you are always with me. (Luke 15:31)
lessons.hook: Tell about a friend who was hurt. “What would make it right?”
lessons.assess: Ask: “What did the father do?”

units.title: Jesus teaches us
units.eq: How does Jesus teach us to live?

lessons.title: The Good Shepherd
lessons.idea: Jesus is the Good Shepherd who knows us and cares for us. He leads us to the Father.
lessons.question: What does a shepherd do for the sheep?
lessons.activity: Make a sheep from cotton balls. Pray Psalm 23 together.
teach: Jesus is the Good Shepherd who knows and loves us (John 10:11–16; CCC 754). He leads us to the Father.
Psalm 23 is a prayer of trust.
Gentle voice.
talk: How does a shepherd care for sheep?
What does it feel like to be known by name?
How does Jesus care for you?
quiz: The Good Shepherd is…|Peter|Noah|Moses|Jesus|3|John 10:11.
The Shepherd knows…|Only the lost|Only some|His sheep by name|No one|2|John 10:3.
Psalm 23 says “The Lord is my…”|King|Teacher|Friend|Shepherd|3|Psalm 23:1.
lessons.life: Pray Psalm 23 before bed this week.
lessons.saint: Patrick: a shepherd boy before he was a missionary.
lessons.mem: The Lord is my shepherd; I shall not want. (Psalm 23:1)
lessons.hook: Hold a toy sheep. “A shepherd knows his sheep by name.”
lessons.assess: Ask children to say the first line of Psalm 23.

lessons.title: Parables of the kingdom
lessons.idea: Jesus told stories to help us know God’s kingdom. The mustard seed and the lost sheep show God’s love.
lessons.question: What do the parables teach us about God?
lessons.activity: Retell the parable of the lost sheep with props.
teach: A parable is a story with a hidden meaning (CCC 546). Mustard seed: the Kingdom starts small and grows (Matthew 13:31–32).
The lost sheep shows God’s love for each one (Luke 15:1–7).
Let children retell stories.
talk: Why did the shepherd leave the 99?
How did he feel when he found the sheep?
Who is the shepherd in your life?
quiz: A parable is…|A prayer|A song|A trick|A story Jesus told|3|CCC 546.
The lost sheep teaches us that God…|Forgets|Searches for us|Is angry|Hides|1|Luke 15:4-7.
The mustard seed is…|Large|Small but grows big|A tree|Useless|1|Matthew 13:31-32.
lessons.life: Look for a way to help someone who feels lost or left out.
lessons.saint: Francis of Assisi: he treated every creature as a gift.
misc: “The Kingdom is a place on a map.”
lessons.mem: The kingdom of heaven is like a mustard seed. (Matthew 13:31)
lessons.hook: Show a tiny seed. “What could it become?”
lessons.assess: Ask children to retell one parable.

lessons.title: The Beatitudes
lessons.idea: Jesus gave us eight ways to be happy. Following them leads us to God.
lessons.question: Which Beatitude is hardest for you?
lessons.activity: Make an eight-sided Beatitudes poster with child-friendly words.
teach: The Beatitudes are Jesus’ ways to be happy (Matthew 5:1–12; CCC 1716–1718).
Child-friendly: happy are those who are kind, who share, who make peace.
Let children illustrate one.
talk: Which Beatitude is easiest for you?
Who in your life lives these?
quiz: The Beatitudes begin with…|Blessed|Beware|Because|Be quiet|0|Matthew 5:3.
Blessed means…|Happy with God|Rich|Famous|Strong|0|CCC 1716.
The Beatitudes were taught on…|A boat|A house|A road|A mountain|3|Matthew 5:1.
lessons.life: Pick one Beatitude to try this week and note what happens.
lessons.saint: Francis and Clare of Assisi: they lived poverty of spirit.
lessons.mem: Blessed are the peacemakers. (Matthew 5:9)
lessons.hook: Ask, “What makes you happy?” List their answers.
lessons.assess: Ask children to choose one Beatitude and say what it means.

lessons.title: Conscience: our inner guide
lessons.idea: Conscience helps us know right from wrong. We should listen to it and form it with the Church’s teaching.
lessons.question: How do you know something is wrong?
lessons.activity: Make “stop and think” cards with questions to ask before acting.
teach: Conscience is God’s voice helping us know good from evil (Romans 2:14–15; CCC 1776–1777, 1783). It must be trained.
Ask: Is this kind? Is this true? Is this safe?
Do not frighten; a conscience guides us.
talk: How do you know right from wrong?
What do you feel when you do wrong?
quiz: Conscience is…|A friend|A teacher|An inner voice that helps us know right from wrong|A feeling only|2|CCC 1776.
We should…|Ignore it|Follow our conscience and learn what is good|Argue|Hide|1|CCC 1783.
To form conscience, we…|Hide|Guess|Pray and learn|Fight|2|CCC 1785.
lessons.life: Ask “Is this loving?” before you act.
lessons.saint: Thomas More: he followed his conscience.
lessons.mem: Help me do what is right, Lord.
lessons.hook: Say, “Have you ever felt a little voice saying ‘don’t do that’?”
lessons.assess: Ask: “What do you do when your conscience says stop?”

lessons.title: Examining our hearts
lessons.idea: Before Confession we think about what we did and ask God for help. We remember: did I love God, my family and others?
lessons.question: What happens when we do not tell the truth?
lessons.activity: Practice an age-appropriate examination of conscience with prompts.
teach: Before Confession we look at our hearts (Psalm 139:23–24; CCC 1454–1455). Ask: Did I love God? My family? Others?
Use three or four simple questions.
End with God’s mercy.
quiz: An examination of conscience helps us…|Judge others|Remember how we loved|Hide|Count candy|1|CCC 1454.
Before Confession we…|Run|Hide|Eat|Think and pray|3|CCC 1454.
We are sorry because…|It is a rule|We love God|We were caught|We are afraid|1|CCC 1451.
lessons.life: Before bed, think of one good thing and one thing you want to do better.
lessons.saint: Ignatius of Loyola: he taught an evening examen.
lessons.mem: Search me, O God, and know my heart. (Psalm 139:23)
lessons.hook: Hold a flashlight. “We shine a light inside our hearts.”
lessons.assess: Ask children to answer two examination questions.

lessons.title: The sacrament of Reconciliation
lessons.idea: We tell our sins to a priest. He gives us a penance and forgives us in Jesus’ name. We feel God’s peace.
lessons.question: What does the priest say after Confession?
lessons.activity: Walk through the steps of Confession using cards. Practice the Act of Contrition.
teach: Steps: greet, Sign of the Cross, “Bless me, Father, for I have sinned,” tell sins, listen, Act of Contrition, absolution, penance (CCC 1450, 1455, 1480).
The priest cannot tell anyone (the seal).
Practice with an adult play-acting.
talk: What do you say at the beginning?
What penance might the priest give?
quiz: Who forgives in Confession?|Nobody|God, through the priest|A friend|The priest alone|1|CCC 1461.
The priest says the words of…|Thanks|Greetings|Goodbye|Absolution|3|CCC 1449.
Confession is private because of…|Embarrassment|The seal|Habit|A rule of school|1|CCC 1467.
lessons.life: Practice the Act of Contrition each night.
lessons.saint: Padre Pio: he heard confessions for hours.
lessons.mem: O my God, I am heartily sorry for having offended you.
lessons.hook: Show the steps on cards. “Let’s practice so it feels easy.”
lessons.assess: Ask children to name the steps in order.

units.title: Preparing for the Eucharist
units.eq: Who do we receive in Communion?

lessons.title: The Last Supper
lessons.idea: Jesus gave us the Eucharist at the Last Supper. He changed bread and wine into his Body and Blood.
lessons.question: What did Jesus do at the Last Supper?
lessons.activity: Set a simple table. Retell the story with bread and a cup.
teach: At the Last Supper Jesus gave us the Eucharist (Luke 22:14–20; CCC 1337, 1339–1340). He said, “Do this in memory of me.”
Every Mass remembers and makes present the Last Supper and the Cross.
Use reverent actions.
talk: What did Jesus say over the bread?
quiz: At the Last Supper Jesus gave…|A song|His Body and Blood|A map|A speech|1|Luke 22:19.
Jesus said, “Do this in…”|Secret|Memory of me|The morning|Your house|1|Luke 22:19.
The Eucharist means…|Party|Thanksgiving|Lunch|Dinner|1|CCC 1328.
lessons.life: At Mass, listen for the words of Jesus over the bread and wine.
lessons.saint: Thomas Aquinas: wrote hymns to the Eucharist.
lessons.mem: This is my body. This is my blood. (see Luke 22:19–20)
lessons.hook: Set a table with bread and a cup. “Jesus shared a special meal with his friends.”
lessons.assess: Ask: “What did Jesus do at the Last Supper?”

lessons.title: Jesus is truly present
lessons.idea: After the priest says the words, bread and wine become Jesus. We call this the Real Presence.
lessons.question: How do we show respect to Jesus in the Eucharist?
lessons.activity: Practice reverent reception, hands and genuflections.
teach: The Real Presence: Jesus is truly there, body, blood, soul and divinity (CCC 1374–1376). Teach slowly.
John 6:51: “I am the living bread.”
Practice reverent reception.
talk: What do you say to Jesus?
quiz: After the consecration, the bread is…|Jesus|Still only bread|A cookie|A symbol|0|CCC 1374.
We call this presence…|Shadow|Pretend|Real Presence|Fake|2|CCC 1374.
We receive Jesus in…|A book|A prayer|A song|Holy Communion|3|CCC 1391.
lessons.life: Make a quiet visit to the church this week and say “Jesus, I believe you are here.”
lessons.saint: Carlo Acutis: he loved the Eucharist.
lessons.mem: Jesus, I believe you are here.
lessons.hook: Hold bread. “How can this be Jesus? We believe because he said so.”
lessons.assess: Ask: “Who is in the Eucharist?”

lessons.title: The parts of the Mass
lessons.idea: The Mass has four parts: gathering, God’s word, the Eucharist and sending forth.
lessons.question: What do we do at each part of Mass?
lessons.activity: Order cards of the Mass, then play a “what comes next” game.
teach: Four parts: gathering, God’s word, the Eucharist, sending forth (CCC 1346, 1348–1355). Link to Emmaus (Luke 24).
Practice responses: “Thanks be to God.”
Take children on a church tour.
quiz: Mass begins with…|The Entrance|Communion|The sermon|The blessing|0|CCC 1348.
We hear readings in…|The Dismissal|The Preface|The Liturgy of the Word|Communion|2|CCC 1349.
Mass ends with…|The Gospel|The blessing and dismissal|The Creed|The Gloria|1|CCC 1332.
lessons.life: Use the Mass mode with your family at Mass this week.
lessons.saint: Pope Pius X: he encouraged frequent Communion for children.
lessons.mem: Lord, have mercy. Christ, have mercy. Lord, have mercy.
lessons.hook: Lay out cards of the four parts. “Mass has a shape.”
lessons.assess: Ask children to arrange the parts of Mass.

lessons.title: Mary says yes
lessons.idea: Mary said yes to God’s plan. We ask her to help us say yes. She is our mother.
lessons.question: What did Mary say at the wedding in Cana?
lessons.activity: Learn the Magnificat’s first lines. Draw Mary at Cana.
teach: Mary said yes to God (Luke 1:38; CCC 488, 494). At Cana she said, “Do whatever he tells you” (John 2:5).
She is our mother (CCC 969). Teach the first lines of the Magnificat.
Keep Mary pointing to Jesus.
talk: How can you say yes to God?
quiz: Mary said…|Later|Let it be done to me|No|Maybe|1|Luke 1:38.
At Cana Mary said…|Wait|Go home|Be quiet|Do whatever he tells you|3|John 2:5.
Mary is our…|Friend only|Mother|Enemy|Boss|1|John 19:27.
lessons.life: Say “Yes, God” when you do a chore this week.
lessons.saint: Bernadette: Mary spoke to her at Lourdes.
lessons.mem: My soul magnifies the Lord. (Luke 1:46)
lessons.hook: Tell about a time someone asked for your help. “What did you say?”
lessons.assess: Ask: “What did Mary say yes to?”

lessons.title: Saints show the way
lessons.idea: Saints loved God in everyday ways. We can follow their examples.
lessons.question: Which saint do you want to be like?
lessons.activity: Create a saint “trading card” with name, feast day, a virtue and a prayer.
teach: Saints loved God in everyday ways (CCC 828, 2030). Their lives show how to follow Jesus.
Include name, feast day, a virtue and a prayer.
Choose saints from many cultures.
talk: How can you pray with your saint?
quiz: Saints show us…|How to be famous|How to follow Jesus|How to win|How to hide|1|CCC 828.
The communion of saints includes…|Only popes|All holy people|Only angels|Only monks|1|CCC 946.
We celebrate saints on…|None|Birthdays only|Feast days|Mondays|2|CCC 1173.
lessons.life: Learn the feast day of your patron saint and celebrate it.
lessons.saint: Your patron: look up your baptismal saint or name saint.
lessons.mem: Be holy, for I am holy. (1 Peter 1:16)
lessons.hook: Show baseball cards. “We make saint cards to remember heroes of faith.”
lessons.assess: Ask children to present a saint card.

lessons.title: Heaven is our home
lessons.idea: Heaven is life with God forever. Jesus has prepared a place for us. We try to follow him there.
lessons.question: What do you think heaven is like?
lessons.activity: Describe heaven in a drawing without trying to “draw God.”
teach: Heaven is life with God forever (CCC 1023–1024, 1026). Jesus prepares a place for us (John 14:1–3).
Avoid boring images (clouds and harps).
Be gentle with grief; heaven is hope.
talk: What do you think heaven is like?
Who do you hope to see?
How do we get ready for heaven?
quiz: Heaven is…|A place with toys|A story|Life with God forever|A dream|2|CCC 1024.
Jesus has prepared…|Nothing|A place for us|A school|A boat|1|John 14:2.
To get to heaven, we…|Love God and others|Hide|Buy|Win|0|Matthew 25.
lessons.life: Pray for someone who has died.
lessons.saint: Bl. Chiara Badano: she said “Yes” to God even in illness.
misc: “I have to be perfect to go.”
lessons.mem: I go to prepare a place for you. (John 14:2)
lessons.hook: Say, “Imagine a home where everyone loves you.” Heaven is even better.
lessons.assess: Ask: “Who is in heaven?”

units.title: The Ten Commandments
units.eq: How do we love God and our neighbor?

lessons.title: Love God first
lessons.idea: The first three commandments teach us to love God: worship him alone, use his name with respect, keep Sunday holy.
lessons.question: Why is God’s name holy?
lessons.activity: Match the first three commandments with actions and examples.
teach: The first three commandments: love God, respect his name, keep Sunday holy (CCC 2052, 2083, 2142, 2168).
Commandments are guides for love.
Link to prayer and Mass.
talk: Why do we use God’s name with respect?
What do we do on Sunday?
quiz: The first commandment: “I am the Lord your God. You shall have…”|No other gods before me|A king|Two gods|Many gods|0|Exodus 20:3.
Keep holy the…|Weekend|Week|Night|Lord’s Day|3|Exodus 20:8.
God’s name is…|Holy|Funny|Secret|Common|0|CCC 2142.
lessons.life: Say “Jesus” with respect and never in anger.
lessons.saint: Moses: he received the commandments.
lessons.mem: You shall love the Lord your God with all your heart. (Deuteronomy 6:5)
lessons.hook: Show a family rules chart. “Rules from a loving Father.”
lessons.assess: Ask children to match each commandment with an action.

lessons.title: Honor your parents and respect life
lessons.idea: The next commandments teach us to honor our parents, respect life and speak the truth.
lessons.question: How can we honor our family?
lessons.activity: Make a family “thank you” poster. Role-play kind speech.
teach: Honor your father and mother (CCC 2197, 2214–2220). Do not kill; respect life (CCC 2258). Tell the truth (CCC 2464).
Honor includes thanks, care, respect.
Be sensitive about family situations.
talk: How can you honor your family?
quiz: Honor your…|Pets|Father and mother|Friends only|Teachers only|1|Exodus 20:12.
Do not…|Kill|Share|Sing|Help|0|Exodus 20:13.
Do not bear false…|Candles|Witness|Gifts|Notes|1|Exodus 20:16.
lessons.life: Thank your parents for something specific.
lessons.saint: Gianna Molla: she gave her life for her child.
lessons.mem: Honor your father and mother. (Exodus 20:12)
lessons.hook: Show photos of grandparents. “Honor means more than obey.”
lessons.assess: Ask children to name three ways to honor family.

lessons.title: Be grateful and content
lessons.idea: The last commandments teach us to be pure of heart, not to steal and not to envy.
lessons.question: What do you have that you can be thankful for?
lessons.activity: Make a gratitude list and a “share with others” jar.
teach: Do not steal; do not envy; keep your heart pure (CCC 2401, 2514, 2534). Gratitude counters envy.
Share with others.
Never shame.
talk: What do you have that you can thank God for?
How do you feel when you envy?
quiz: Do not…|Share|Steal|Thank|Pray|1|Exodus 20:15.
Do not covet…|Free things|Your neighbor’s goods|Anything|Your own|1|Exodus 20:17.
Gratitude is…|Greed|Thankfulness|Envy|Anger|1|CCC 2637.
lessons.life: Write three thanks each night.
lessons.saint: Francis of Assisi: he embraced poverty and joy.
lessons.mem: Give thanks in all circumstances. (1 Thessalonians 5:18)
lessons.hook: Show a jar for thank-yous. “Gratitude fills our hearts.”
lessons.assess: Ask children to list three things they are thankful for.

units.title: Prayer
units.eq: How do we grow close to God?

lessons.title: Our Father
lessons.idea: The Our Father is the prayer Jesus taught. It has seven requests.
lessons.question: What do we ask for in the Our Father?
lessons.activity: Illustrate each petition with a picture.
teach: Seven requests (CCC 2759, 2761, 2765). First three are about God, last four about us.
Give a simple picture for each.
Pray it together daily.
quiz: The Our Father has…|Two|Seven petitions|Ten|Twelve|1|CCC 2759.
“Give us this day our…”|Daily bread|Time|Wishes|Toys|0|Matthew 6:11.
“Deliver us from…”|Evil|Sleep|School|Work|0|Matthew 6:13.
lessons.life: Pray the Our Father slowly and think of what you are asking.
lessons.saint: Teresa of Avila: she wrote about the Our Father.
lessons.mem: Give us this day our daily bread, and forgive us our trespasses as we forgive those who trespass against us.
lessons.hook: Say the Our Father slowly with a gesture. “What do these words ask?”
lessons.assess: Ask children to explain one petition.

lessons.title: Prayers of the Church
lessons.idea: We pray the Hail Mary, Glory Be, Apostles’ Creed and Act of Contrition. We memorize them to pray anywhere.
lessons.question: Which prayer do you know by heart?
lessons.activity: Play a memory game with the basic prayers.
teach: The Hail Mary, Glory Be, Apostles’ Creed and Act of Contrition are prayers of the Church (CCC 2676, 2698).
Repeat and review often.
Prayer is relationship, not performance.
talk: Which prayer do you know by heart?
quiz: The Apostles’ Creed begins…|I believe in God|Glory be|Hail Mary|Our Father|0|CCC 194.
The Glory Be praises…|Mary|The Trinity|Saints|Angels|1|CCC 2639.
The Act of Contrition expresses…|Anger|Joy|Fear|Sorrow|3|CCC 1451.
lessons.life: Learn one new prayer each week.
lessons.saint: Thérèse: she loved simple prayers.
lessons.mem: Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit, as it was in the beginning, is now, and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.
lessons.hook: Play a memory game with prayer cards.
lessons.assess: Ask children to say a prayer they know by heart.

lessons.title: Quiet time with God
lessons.idea: We can pray in silence and listen to God. This is meditation.
lessons.question: What can you hear when it is quiet?
lessons.activity: Practice a minute of silence. Take turns saying, “Speak, Lord, your servant is listening.”
teach: Meditation is quiet listening (Psalm 46:10; CCC 2705, 2708, 2710). Samuel heard God’s voice (1 Samuel 3:1–10).
Start with 30 seconds.
No pressure.
talk: What can you hear when it’s quiet?
What do you want to say to God?
quiz: Meditation is…|Noise|Sleep|Exercise|Quiet prayer|3|CCC 2705.
Samuel said…|Go away|No|Speak, Lord|Later|2|1 Samuel 3:10.
God listens…|Only at church|Always|Never|Sometimes|1|Psalm 34:15.
lessons.life: Spend one minute in silence each day.
lessons.saint: Mary: she pondered things in her heart.
lessons.mem: Speak, Lord, your servant is listening. (1 Samuel 3:9)
lessons.hook: Ask for silence for ten seconds. “What do you hear?”
lessons.assess: Ask children to be quiet for one minute and share one thing.

units.title: The Church year
units.eq: How does the Church help us follow Jesus all year?

lessons.title: Advent and Christmas
lessons.idea: We prepare for Jesus’ birth and then celebrate it for many days.
lessons.question: What do we do in Advent to prepare?
lessons.activity: Create an Advent calendar with acts of love.
teach: Advent prepares for Christmas; Christmas lasts to the Baptism of the Lord (CCC 524–525, 1171).
Do acts of kindness.
Keep the season distinct.
talk: How can you prepare your heart?
quiz: Advent lasts about…|Four weeks|Ten days|One week|Two months|0|CCC 524.
Advent candles are…|Red|Purple and pink|Gold|Blue|1|Liturgy.
We wait for…|Jesus|A party|A gift only|A trip|0|CCC 524.
lessons.life: Do one act of kindness each day in Advent.
lessons.saint: Mary and Joseph: they waited and prepared.
lessons.mem: Come, Lord Jesus.
lessons.hook: Light the wreath. “We prepare our hearts.”
lessons.assess: Ask children to name one Advent practice.

lessons.title: Lent and Easter
lessons.idea: In Lent we pray, fast and give. At Easter we celebrate that Jesus is alive.
lessons.question: What can we give up or share?
lessons.activity: Choose a small Lenten promise.
teach: In Lent we pray, fast and give (Matthew 6:1–18; CCC 538, 1438). Easter celebrates that Jesus is alive (CCC 1169).
Choose a small promise.
Easter lasts fifty days.
quiz: Lent lasts…|Seven days|Ten days|Forty days|One month|2|CCC 540.
During Lent we…|Party|Forget|Travel|Pray, fast, give|3|Matthew 6.
Easter celebrates…|The Resurrection|Pentecost|The birth|The ascension|0|CCC 638.
lessons.life: Choose a Lenten promise and tell your family.
lessons.saint: Francis: he lived simply.
lessons.mem: Jesus is risen, alleluia!
lessons.hook: Show ashes and a candle. “Lent and Easter.”
lessons.assess: Ask: “What is your Lenten promise?”

lessons.title: Holy days and feasts
lessons.idea: We celebrate feasts of Mary and the saints and holy days like All Saints.
lessons.question: What is your favorite feast?
lessons.activity: Mark your family’s feast days on a calendar.
teach: Feast days celebrate Mary, the saints and mysteries (CCC 1172, 2043). All Saints Nov. 1; All Souls Nov. 2.
Mark your family’s feast days.
Revelation 7:9: a great multitude.
talk: How can we celebrate at home?
